response.justification: The candidate is an accomplished full-stack/web engineer with 15+ years of experience, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect role in AI accelerator silicon. There is no evidence of SoC or IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, computer architecture work, deep-learning workload analysis, GPU/SIMD/MIMD experience, or system architecture for accelerators. The closest adjacent work is low-latency service optimization in D at Sociomantic and some C/C++ component work at National Instruments, which is far from silicon performance modeling. Education is a BS in Computer Science (meets the 8+ years experience path formally), but the domain expertise gap is too large to close in a principal-level IC hire.
strengths: 15+ years of broad, senior-level software engineering experience
Low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/s in D)
Some systems/C++ and embedded exposure; strong OSS and teaching record
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or computer architecture experience
No deep-learning training/inference or GPU/accelerator workload expertise
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture background
No AI/deep-learning workload or GPU optimization experience
Extensive senior software engineering and performance-sensitive systems work
